one_month_reasoning: Qualcomm's fiscal Q4 FY26 report is expected in the first half of November (data sites show Nov 4-11), i.e. most likely just after the 2026-10-30 window closes, so the main company catalyst is outside the window. Inside the window: TrendForce's 4Q26 memory outlook (DRAM +10-15% QoQ, NAND +15-20%) keeps handset cost pressure in the news; TSMC mid-October results, Samsung/SK hynix late-October results (memory pricing), Apple and MediaTek late-October results (iPhone mix, Android flagship ramp: MediaTek August revenue was a record on flagship SoC ramp), and first Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 phone launches in China. These are mixed and mostly already known. The stock just fell ~9% in two sessions (Sep 28-29) after a ~35% Amazon/Apple-license rally from ~$145, so short-horizon reversal and momentum roughly offset. I therefore stay near a symmetric distribution around $184.5 with monthly sigma ~14% (slightly below 54%/3.5 = 15.4% because no earnings print is in the window).

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E on core earnings (NTM EPS ~$9.30 consensus, stepped to ~$9.8 for the Sep-2027 forward year, x 18.5x = $181) and a sum-of-parts (core handset/auto/IoT/QTL at 15x $9.3 = $140 plus ~$42/share for the data-center/Amazon option, net of warrant dilution = $182).

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus NTM $9.30 rolled forward ~5%: handset units still down (IDC -16.7% 2026, memory tight into 2028) and Apple chip revenue near zero by the 2027 iPhone, offset by auto (+61% YoY), IoT and custom data-center silicon that management says starts shipping in the December quarter, plus Snapdragon price increases.

Stock trades ~20x NTM today (up from ~19x in June) after the Amazon deal; I use slightly below current because handset cycle trough is not yet visible and Street mean target ($194) implies ~21x, while a pure handset-SoC multiple would be ~14-15x.

Ex-AI handset/licensing business in a record unit contraction (IDC, Counterpoint) with Apple and Samsung (S27 ~50% Snapdragon) share losses: discount to the 19-20x the whole company trades at.

inputs_detail.derivation: Management's ~$5B FY27 data-center revenue target plus Humain 200MW; at ~25% operating margin that is ~$1.0B after-tax earnings growing fast, valued at ~40x to reflect multi-year Amazon runway but heavy execution risk and the fact that the $60B is a warrant ceiling, not a commitment.
1.057B outstanding plus the 25M Amazon warrant if fully vested.

bear.story: Memory shortage persists through 2027 (IDC sees constraint to 2028); Android units keep falling, Samsung S27 Snapdragon share drops to ~50%, Apple chip revenue gone, custom data-center silicon ramps slowly and Amazon purchases stay small. EPS ~$8.3 at 15x.

base.story: Handset trough in calendar 2026-H1 2027, Snapdragon price increases and mix offset units; auto/IoT keep growing double digits; data center delivers a few $B in FY27. Apple licence renewal secures QTL. EPS ~$9.8-10 at ~19x.

bull.story: Amazon custom-silicon and optical interconnect ramp faster, a second hyperscaler win, memory prices plateau in 2027 so Android flagships recover; market re-rates QCOM as an AI-infrastructure name (retest of 52-week high $260). EPS ~$11 at 24x.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$130 (below the post-Q3 low of ~$145 and ~14x trough EPS) the market would be saying either that the Amazon/hyperscaler data-center revenue is not materialising or that the handset business is losing share beyond Apple (e.g. Samsung majority-Exynos, Chinese OEMs shifting to MediaTek) with FY27 EPS heading below $8; that is a fundamental break, not normal 54%-vol noise.

reasoning: Value-chain evidence is mixed. Negative: the handset end market is in its worst contraction on record (IDC Aug-26: 2026 units -16.7%, Android -24%, memory costs +300%, constraint until 2028; Counterpoint Q2-26 shipments at a 13-year low with Xiaomi/Oppo/vivo down double digits), TrendForce still sees DRAM +10-15% and NAND +15-20% QoQ in 4Q26, Samsung is moving the S27 to ~50% Exynos 2700, and Apple's modem share is collapsing (only US Pro Max uses X80; all 2027 iPhones expected on Apple modems). QCOM handset revenue fell 20% YoY in FQ3 and the Street expects December-quarter sales down ~14%. Positive: Qualcomm pushed through double-digit Snapdragon price increases (Gen 6 ~$300+/unit) and flagship ASPs are rising (IDC ASP +27.6%), MediaTek's record August revenue shows flagship SoC demand is holding up at the high end, China handset revenue is said to have bottomed, auto +61%, the Apple patent licence was renewed (protecting QTL), and the Amazon multi-generation custom-silicon/optical deal (warrant up to $60B of purchases) plus Humain give a credible data-center leg. The stock already reflects much of this: it ran from ~$145 after FQ3 to ~$202 and fell back to $184 (about 20x NTM EPS $9.30, Street mean target ~$194). My fair value (~$182, P/E and SOTP) is close to the price, so I centre the 12-month distribution at ~$186 (small drift) with a fat-tailed spread: 80% weight on a 40%-vol lognormal and 20% on a 70%-vol lognormal, reflecting realised vol of 54% inflated by AI-headline spikes but a genuinely binary data-center outcome. Scenario mean (0.28x125 + 0.47x190 + 0.25x265 = $191) is consistent with the ladder. Research was limited to ~14 queries; no option data used.
